stories.title: Kiosk GPU-raster fix -- drop --enable-gpu-rasterization to kill the freeze class
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #1 -- CORRECTED PREMISE 2026-08-02, design-gate] --enable-gpu-rasterization is NOT in the repo or the eclipse-dashboard unit; it is a Debian/RPi-OS system default injected by the /usr/bin/chromium-browser wrapper from /etc/chromium.d/default-flags:7. FIX = ADD an override flag to the eclipse-dashboard unit ExecStart (deploy-pi.sh, repo-managed): --disable-gpu-rasterization (keep GL compositing) OR --disable-gpu (bulletproof software render, removes the whole GPU-command-buffer path). Atlas leans --disable-gpu (the Pi CPU trivially handles this 2D card UI; removes the entire failure class). Eliminates the chromium GPU command-buffer hot-loop (AllocateRingBuffer kFatalFailure, ~6M/boot) that froze the UI. RCA: offices/architect/findings/2026-08-02-pi-ui-freeze-chromium-gpu-command-buffer-hotloop.md

[PRECEDENCE -- verify, do NOT assume] the Debian wrapper runs `chromium $CHROMIUM_FLAGS "$@"`, so the ExecStart override SHOULD win over the injected default -- but VERIFY on the Pi (a wrapper-ordering surprise = silent mocked-green / IRL-miss)

[A-16 deploy-contract blind spot] chromium's base flags live in an OS-shipped /etc/chromium.d/ file the repo does not manage; add a one-line comment in deploy-pi.sh so a future chromium package upgrade re-introducing GPU raster is a known surface
installs via the existing cmp-guarded kiosk-unit step + daemon-reload; ruff/lint clean in-loop

[Atlas keyring fix 2026-08-03 -- SAME ExecStart as the GPU override] add --password-store=basic to the eclipse-dashboard kiosk ExecStart (both dashboard.service.x11 + .wayland). Root: the kiosk runs with no --password-store -> chromium uses the GNOME keyring for its Safe-Storage key; the password-protected Default keyring stays LOCKED under passwordless auto-login (pam_gnome_keyring never unlocks it), so chromium fires a repeating Authentication Required keyring popup. --password-store=basic keeps safe-storage in chromiums own wiped /tmp profile (no meaningful security downgrade for a kiosk that stores no real passwords). Atlas live-tested on the Pi; repo-unmanaged until this lands.

validationCriteria.action: post-deploy on the Pi, `pgrep -a chromium` to confirm the override wins over /etc/chromium.d, then sustained carousel navigation for several minutes + `journalctl -u eclipse-dashboard | grep -c AllocateRingBuffer`
validationCriteria.outcome: the RUNNING chromium cmdline shows GPU rasterization effectively off (override present + winning), AllocateRingBuffer count stays ~0, chromium CPU low, display never freezes

validationCriteria.action: post-deploy on the Pi, pgrep -a chromium + check for a gcr-prompter/keyring-prompt process
validationCriteria.outcome: the running chromium cmdline shows BOTH --disable-gpu* (GPU fix) AND --password-store=basic effective, and no keyring-authentication popup / gcr-prompter process appears

conditionalOutcomes: if the ExecStart override does NOT win over /etc/chromium.d/default-flags (wrapper-ordering surprise), STOP and escalate to Atlas -- do not assume precedence
if GPU-off alone does NOT eliminate the freeze, escalate -- fix-selection (disable-gpu vs disable-gpu-rasterization vs cma vs animations) is a hypothesis; do not stack blind changes
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the Pi dashboard to never freeze under sustained use, so the display stays live during a drive instead of wedging silently.
stories.completionNotes: FIX = --disable-gpu added to the eclipse-dashboard ExecStart in BOTH kiosk variants (.x11 + .wayland). Atlas's corrected premise CONFIRMED on the live Pi: --enable-gpu-rasterization is nowhere in the repo -- /etc/chromium.d/default-flags exports it and the /usr/bin/chromium wrapper sources it. AC2 PRECEDENCE VERIFIED LIVE, NOT ASSUMED (this was the story's real risk): /usr/bin/chromium:195 runs `exec $LIBDIR/$APPNAME $CHROMIUM_FLAGS "$@"`, so OS flags land FIRST and the unit's argv LAST; the live composed cmdline read exactly `... --enable-gpu-rasterization ... --use-angle=gles --disable-gpu <url>`. So the ExecStart override DOES reach chromium after the injected default -- no wrapper-ordering surprise, no escalation to Atlas needed. FLAG SELECTION took Atlas's lean (--disable-gpu) and it is now evidence-backed rather than preference: (a) the fault is in the GPU COMMAND BUFFER, which COMPOSITING uses as well as raster, so --disable-gpu-rasterization alone shrinks the pressure without removing the mechanism; (b) I enumerated the full injected set live (--show-component-extension-options / --enable-gpu-rasterization / --no-default-browser-check / --disable-pings / --media-router=0 / --enable-remote-extensions / --use-angle=gles / --js-flags=--no-decommit-pooled-pages / --force-renderer-accessibility) and NOTHING in it is --enable-gpu -- so --disable-gpu is unopposed and the fix does not depend on flag ORDER at all, which the narrower flag would. LIVE SMOKE PROBE (non-invasive, the installed unit was never modified): ran the composed flag set against the real dashboard URL on DISPLAY=:0 in a throwaway profile for 12s -- chromium stayed up, 0 AllocateRingBuffer, no GL/fatal init error. Probe fully cleaned up; verified afterwards that only the real kiosk's 9 processes remain, probe files gone, eclipse-dashboard still active. HONEST BOUND: a software-GL gpu-process is STILL present with --disable-gpu, so the claim is that the v3d-on-64MiB-CMA exhaustion mechanism is gone, NOT that no GPU process exists -- do not let the multi-minute drill be read as proving the latter. AC4 install path: the dashboard kit's install.sh substitutes __CHROMIUM_BIN__/__PI_USER__ and unconditionally re-installs the unit + `systemctl daemon-reload` (install.sh:174-193), so a template change DOES reach the Pi on the next deploy; note the cmp-guard in deploy-pi.sh's kiosk step covers the xorg no-blank drop-in, not the unit itself (the unit is idempotent-overwrite, which is equivalent here). SCOPE HELD: the splash kiosk units (specs/UI/dist/splash-pi/splash-boot.service.*, splash-grace.service.*) also launch chromium through the SAME wrapper and therefore ALSO inherit --enable-gpu-rasterization -- deliberately NOT touched (US-522 names the eclipse-dashboard unit). Flagging it for US-525, which is already in the splash: if the splash ever shows the same wedge, that is why. PM/INTEGRATION GATE: no full-suite risk from this change (2 systemd templates + a bash comment + one test file), but tests/lint carries the pre-existing TD-073 red (US-529's job) and I filed TD-075 for 10 pre-existing project-wide ruff errors in files this story does not touch (src/calibration/speed_aligner-spool.py + tests/pm/*) -- `ruff check src/ tests/` therefore exits 1 on a clean tree, which is why DoD 'make lint clean' was applied per-touched-file. IN-LOOP GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY: tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py 54 passed, full tests/deploy 379 passed, ruff clean on tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py. RED witnessed before GREEN (2 of 6 new guards failed for the right reasons). === REOPEN CLOSE 2026-08-03 (AC5, Atlas keyring fix) === --password-store=basic added to BOTH kiosk variants' ExecStart (.x11 + .wayland) with the rationale in the .x11 header and a pointer in .wayland. BL-029 IS CLEARED (PM commit 0f40705) -- the stale .git/index.lock is gone and this story's work IS COMMITTED (2412227), unlike US-525's first pass. AC5's premise VERIFIED LIVE, NOT ASSUMED, and the verification did real work: the journal shows gcr-prompter PerformPrompt firing at Aug 03 05:43:09, 08:33:52 AND 08:52:23 -- so the popup genuinely RECURS as the AC claims, and post-fix chromium logs `key_storage_linux.cc:116 Selected backend for OSCrypt: BASIC_TEXT` + `OSCrypt did not initialize a backend`, i.e. the flag demonstrably takes the keyring out of the path. Root cause confirmed on the box: ~/.local/share/keyrings/Default_Keyring.keyring exists at 0600 (password-protected) with gnome-keyring-daemon --components=pkcs11,secrets running under passwordless auto-login. SCOPE QUESTION ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the splash units launch chromium through the SAME wrapper with no --password-store, so 'is the dashboard-only fix complete?' was a real question. The timeline settles it -- every observed prompt is ~9h AFTER splash-boot exited (Aug 02 20:20:21) and NONE fired inside the splash's own 9.806s window, so the prompts track the LONG-RUNNING dashboard chromium and AC5's dashboard-only scope is correct AND sufficient for the observed defect. Filed TD-076 rather than widening scope, and the TD carries the non-obvious half: 'the splash is short-lived' only holds on a HEALTHY boot -- per the A-1 contract a DEGRADED boot deliberately KEEPS THE SPLASH UP, which is exactly the long-running case that produced the dashboard's popup, so on a degraded boot a keyring dialog can paint over the one screen the operator most needs to read. UNPLANNED FINDING THE PM/DEPLOY SHOULD KNOW -- THE LIVE UNIT IS DRIFTED FROM THE REPO: the installed /etc/systemd/system/eclipse-dashboard.service is a PRE-US-522 copy (its header has no US-522 section) that was HAND-PATCHED, with four flags appended onto one line: `--password-store=basic --disable-gpu-rasterization --enable-logging=stderr --remote-debugging-port=9222`. So (a) the deploy has not run since US-522 landed, consistent with US-524's independent finding that set-gpu-cma.sh is not on the box; (b) Atlas live-tested the keyring fix ALONGSIDE --disable-gpu-rasterization, NOT alongside the repo's --disable-gpu -- the two fixes are orthogonal (OSCrypt backend vs GPU command buffer) so this does not undermine the keyring result, but the shipped combination is NOT the exact combination that was live-tested, and validationCriteria #2 was written with a --disable-gpu* wildcard for that reason; (c) on the next deploy install.sh overwrites the unit, so --disable-gpu-rasterization/--enable-logging/--remote-debugging-port ALL disappear and --disable-gpu + --password-store=basic take effect. DELIBERATELY DID NOT ADOPT THE DEBUG FLAGS that sat beside the one being adopted: --remote-debugging-port=9222 on a car-mounted kiosk is unauthenticated full-page DevTools control, and --enable-logging=stderr was Atlas's aid for reading the OSCrypt line. A test FENCES --remote-debugging-* so it cannot arrive later by copy-paste from the box. Note the trade-off honestly: without --enable-logging the OSCrypt confirmation line will NOT appear in the journal on the deployed unit, which is why validationCriteria #2 correctly reads `pgrep -a chromium` + absence of a gcr-prompter process instead of grepping for the log line. GUARDS ARE VALUE-BASED, NOT PREFIX-BASED, and that is the story's mutation trap: --password-store is a VALUED switch, so `'--password-store' in flags` passes on --password-store=gnome -- the broken config -- exactly as US-522's first pass found --disable-gpu is a substring of --disable-gpu-rasterization. The helper returns the VALUE LIST and a dedicated fence asserts the value is `basic`, never gnome/gnome-libsecret/kwallet. MUTATION-PROVED on the real artifact (not just the synthetic self-test): flipping the wayland unit basic->gnome turned 3 guards red including the never-keyring-backed fence, then reverted and re-verified green. LIVE VALIDATION STILL OWED, NOT FAKED: validationCriteria #2 needs a PM deploy (handbook 13) -- after it, `pgrep -a chromium` should show BOTH --disable-gpu and --password-store=basic with no gcr-prompter process. It cannot be claimed from here because the box is still running the hand-patched pre-US-522 unit. IN-LOOP GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY: RED witnessed first (2 of 5 new guards failed for the right reason -- missing flag); then tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py 59 passed and the FULL tests/deploy 410 passed with ZERO SKIPS (both unit templates changed = the whole deploy contract ran; skip count read deliberately per US-524). ruff clean on tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py. stories.title: Kiosk watchdog -- auto-restart eclipse-dashboard when the renderer wedges
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #2] add a watchdog that detects a wedged renderer (e.g. AllocateRingBuffer error-rate spike, or a CPU-pegged chromium with no state-file-driven repaint) and restarts eclipse-dashboard to restore a fresh GPU context (the proven live mitigation)

conservative trigger: restart only on a genuine wedge, never flap under normal operation; log every restart so recurring wedges stay visible (defense-in-depth behind US-522, must not mask a still-present freeze class)
test proves the watchdog triggers a restart on a simulated wedge and no-ops under healthy operation; ruff clean in-loop

validationCriteria.action: simulate/observe a renderer wedge on the Pi
validationCriteria.outcome: eclipse-dashboard is auto-restarted and the display recovers with no human intervention; the restart is logged

conditionalOutcomes: watchdog is defense-in-depth, NOT the primary fix (US-522). It must surface recurring wedges, not silence them.
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the kiosk to recover itself if the renderer ever wedges, so the display never stays silently frozen (honest-instrument).
stories.completionNotes: SHAPE: deploy/eclipse-kiosk-watchdog.{service,timer} (30s Type=oneshot) + src/pi/display/kiosk_watchdog.py + a cmp-guarded deploy-pi.sh step called AFTER step_install_ui_kiosk_units. One tick = count 'AllocateRingBuffer' markers in eclipse-dashboard's journal over a 60s window; at >=100, `systemctl restart eclipse-dashboard.service` -- the exact mitigation Atlas proved live (fresh GPU context, markers back to 0). AC1 SIGNAL CHOICE, and it is a REFUSAL not an omission: the AC offered 'AllocateRingBuffer error-rate spike, OR a CPU-pegged chromium with no state-file-driven repaint'. I built ONLY the first. 'No repaint' is NOT observable from outside the browser (states_http_server silences per-request logging, so there is no access log to read a renderer heartbeat from, and I would not widen that token-gated server while US-525 is also in it), and the CPU half alone has no post-US-522 baseline: Atlas's 39/31/24%-wedged vs 18/9/8%-healthy figures predate --disable-gpu, and software rendering raises healthy CPU by an amount nobody has measured. A CPU threshold today would be a fabricated number (Rule 2), so the honest bound is stated in the module header, the architecture section and here: A WEDGE WITH A DIFFERENT SIGNATURE IS NOT DETECTED. If the CIO wants that coverage, the cheap grounded path is to read healthy chromium CPU during the US-522 multi-minute drill and then threshold against it -- or add a renderer heartbeat (page-side, Iris) which would make 'no repaint' genuinely observable. GROUNDING for the numbers: threshold 100/60s sits ~300x below the measured wedge rate (~500/s = ~30,000 per window) and above the measured healthy 0; window 60s follows Atlas's 2,500-per-5s figure; tick 30s = half the window (a wedge is recovered inside ~1.5 min vs the 4:42 the bench sat frozen); cooldown 180s > window so a tick can never see a pre-restart error; budget 5/hour is a stated POLICY choice, not a measurement. All five are CLI flags, so the unit retunes without a code change. AC2 NEVER-FLAP, six rules each with its own test: (1) an INACTIVE kiosk is left alone -- `systemctl restart` STARTS an inactive unit, which would usurp the splash OnSuccess hand-off (dashboard.service.x11 A-1, no [Install] by design); (2) an unreadable journal is UNCERTAIN, never a wedge (I-037); (3) the journal window is max(now-window, lastAttempt) so the errors that justified a restart cannot re-trigger the next tick; (4) cooldown; (5) an hourly restart BUDGET -- once spent the watchdog STOPS restarting, logs ERROR and exits 2 so systemd marks the unit FAILED; (6) the attempt is written to the tmpfs ledger BEFORE the restart fires, so an unwritable ledger CANCELS the restart rather than silently uncapping rules 3-5. AC2 'must not mask a still-present freeze class' is met structurally, not just by a log line: every restart logs at WARNING and says in-line that US-522 was supposed to have removed this class, and the budget converts a recurring wedge into a persistent visible FAILED unit instead of an invisible restart loop. FOOT-GUN CAUGHT + GUARDED: the ledger dir is the watchdog's OWN RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-kiosk-watchdog + RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes. Declaring RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-obd would have made systemd DELETE /run/eclipse-obd -- including the live states/ every emitter writes and the state server reads -- every 30s when this oneshot exits; and without Preserve=yes the ledger would evaporate each fire, leaving cooldown+budget permanently empty = a restart every tick. Both are pinned by tests and MUTATION-PROVED (I mutated the unit to RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-obd + Wants=eclipse-dashboard, watched exactly those two guards go red, then reverted and re-verified clean). PRIVILEGE: unprivileged (User=mcornelison) -- the restart rides the EXISTING polkit grant in deploy/polkit-rules/51-eclipse-service-control.rules (restart verb on eclipse-dashboard.service) so NO new privilege is added, plus SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal so the journal read does not depend on journald's per-uid file split. That polkit grant is a two-correct-halves hazard (revoke it and every watchdog test stays green while recovery is dead on the Pi), so a test pins it. RULE 10: specs/architecture.md dashboard-kiosk section gains a 'Kiosk freeze class + wedge recovery' subsection covering BOTH US-522 (override-not-deletion, /etc/chromium.d surface -- US-522 shipped without a spec update, so this closes that too) and US-523, and I amended the A-1 hand-off paragraph, which flatly said 'No watchdog/timer' -- still true as written (nothing STARTS the dashboard) but it would read as a contradiction to the next person. SCOPE: unit_manifest.py deliberately NOT touched -- it consistently excludes timer-driven oneshots (drain-forensics, orphan-cleanup, boot-progress are all absent), so following that precedent is the non-drift choice; if PM/Atlas want the watchdog in `obdctl status all` that is a separate call. LIVE VALIDATION STILL OWED (validationCriteria = simulate/observe a wedge on the Pi): I could not exercise it on the box this iteration and did NOT fake it. Note for whoever runs it: with US-522 in place a NATURAL wedge should be unreproducible, so the drill is `--error-threshold 1` against any journal marker, or a synthetic marker via systemd-cat, and the meaningful assertion is that the restart happens, is logged, and the ledger caps repeats. GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP: RED witnessed first (module absent -> ImportError); then tests/pi/display/test_kiosk_watchdog.py 43 passed, tests/deploy/test_kiosk_watchdog_install.py 18 passed, FULL tests/deploy 397 passed (I changed deploy-pi.sh, so the whole suite for that contract ran), tests/pi/ops green, ruff clean on all 3 touched Python files. PRE-EXISTING RED, NOT MINE: tests/lint/test_ralph_promise_tag_contract.py (TD-073) -- US-529 in this same sprint. TD-075 (10 project-wide ruff errors outside touched files) also still stands, so `make lint` clean was applied per-touched-file; `make` is not on PATH on this box, use `ruff check` directly.

stories.title: Raise Pi GPU CMA to 256M -- headroom complementing the raster fix
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #4 -- optional headroom, complements US-522, NOT a standalone fix] raise the Pi CMA pool to cma=256M (boot cmdline/config). Box-config change: confirm the mechanism (config.txt/cmdline.txt on the Pi boot partition) and whether deploy-pi.sh can write it within scope
verify post-boot CmaTotal reflects the raise (was 65536 kB)

validationCriteria.outcome: CmaTotal ~262144 kB (256 MiB), up from 65536 kB

conditionalOutcomes: if the boot-config change is outside Ralph's deploy write-scope (bootloader/ownership), emit a one-line CIO ops instruction instead of forcing it into the deploy script -- do not half-apply
stories.goal: As the operator, I want more GPU command-buffer headroom on the Pi, so the compositor has margin under sustained animated use.
stories.completionNotes: TD-059 STALL RECOVERY, NOT A RE-IMPLEMENTATION -- read this first. I booted into a tree where the implementation was ALREADY COMMITTED (e78c51e, 4 files, 724 insertions) but every piece of bookkeeping was missing: sprint.json still said sprint-ready/passes:false, progress.txt had no US-524 entry, ralph_agents.json still showed me active on it. That is the exact TD-059 shape US-505 documented (work done, synchronous gate + close dropped at the END of the iteration) and it is now the SIXTH sighting across sprints 69-70. Per the US-505 rule I re-ran the gate and VERIFIED rather than re-implementing. AC1 MECHANISM -- CONFIRMED LIVE, and the answer was NOT the one the AC's wording assumed: the AC says 'boot cmdline/config' and offers config.txt OR cmdline.txt. On the live Pi (10.27.27.100, Pi 5 Rev 1.1) /proc/cmdline carries NO cma= arg at all -- the 64 MiB pool comes from the DEVICE TREE (dmesg: 'created CMA memory pool ... size 64 MiB' against the linux,cma reserved-memory node) -- and /boot/firmware/config.txt holds a bare `dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d` at line 26. So the mechanism is the OVERLAY PARAM (cma-256, documented in the Pi's own /boot/firmware/overlays/README as cma-64..cma-512), not a cmdline edit. That choice is also the RECOVERABLE one and that is why it was taken: a bad overlay param makes the firmware skip the overlay (dark display, SSH still up) whereas a malformed cmdline.txt can break root= and leave an UNBOOTABLE HEADLESS box. A guard pins that cmdline.txt is never touched. AC1 SECOND HALF -- deploy-pi.sh CAN write it within scope, so the conditionalOutcome escape hatch ('emit a one-line CIO ops instruction instead') was correctly NOT taken: there is an exact precedent in step_enforce_eeprom_power_off_on_halt (US-253), a standalone sudo'd idempotent script re-asserted on EVERY deploy. step_set_gpu_cma mirrors it verbatim and is ordered directly after it, both AFTER sync_tree so the script exists on the Pi. Re-asserting every deploy is the point, not redundancy: config.txt is OS-shipped and rewritable out-of-band by rpi-update / an image upgrade / raspi-config -- the same unmanaged-boot-surface class as US-522's /etc/chromium.d note (A-16). NEW VERIFICATION I ADDED THIS ITERATION (the original commit did not have it): I ran set-gpu-cma.sh against a COPY of the live Pi's REAL config.txt, not only my synthetic fixtures. This matters because the real file turns out to contain [cm4], [cm5] (with its own dtoverlay=dwc2,dr_mode=host) and [all] sections -- so the script's section-scoping logic is LIVE-RELEVANT, not hypothetical: config.txt is section-conditional, and appending cma to a line under [cm4] would be a false 'applied' claim on a Pi 5. Result against the real file: applied cleanly at line 26 -> `dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d,cma-256`; idempotent no-op on re-run; backup pristine (no cma); and the [cm5] dwc2 overlay UNTOUCHED, which is the proof it does not spray cma- onto unrelated overlays. Probe ran on a COPY only -- the Pi's real boot config was never modified (read-only `cat` was the only remote op) -- and all four temp files were deleted + the deletion verified. AC2 IS GENUINELY OWED, AND I DID NOT FAKE IT: 'verify post-boot CmaTotal reflects the raise' needs the deploy + a REBOOT, and deploying is PM-owned (handbook 13), not Ralph's. I probed read-only and report the honest current state: the Pi is STILL at CmaTotal 65536 kB, the overlay line is still bare, and ~/obd2/deploy/set-gpu-cma.sh does not yet exist on the box -- i.e. the deploy has not run. The story ships the repo-managed mechanism; the drill (deploy -> reboot -> `grep CmaTotal /proc/meminfo`, expect ~262144 kB) closes AC2. The script prints exactly that command and that expected number, and deliberately says REBOOT REQUIRED rather than implying the pool was raised immediately -- claiming otherwise would be a confident lie about a value anyone can read. HONEST BOUND ON THE STORY ITSELF: this is Atlas RCA #4, OPTIONAL HEADROOM. It is NOT a fix for the freeze class -- US-522's --disable-gpu is. Do not read a green US-524 as 'the freeze is fixed', and note the interaction: with --disable-gpu the kiosk renders in software, so a larger CMA pool may show no measurable effect on chromium at all. The value of the raise is margin for the KMS/display stack generally, and I am not claiming a measured benefit nobody has measured. GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP: tests/deploy/test_set_gpu_cma.py 8 passed (no skips -- bash IS on PATH here, and a skip would have silently voided the whole behavioural catalog); the bash catalog run directly = 35 assertions passed / 0 failed over 12 scenarios; FULL tests/deploy 405 passed (deploy-pi.sh changed, so the whole contract suite ran, same posture as US-522/523); ruff clean on tests/deploy/test_set_gpu_cma.py. stories.completionNotes: *** READ FIRST: THE WORK IS COMPLETE AND GATE-GREEN BUT UNCOMMITTED. *** A stale 0-byte .git/index.lock (created 08:26, still there 13+ min later) blocks every `git add` on the shared checkout. I retried 4 times, then declined to force it: handbook 13 rule 4 forbids deleting the lock while a git process runs, and I could NOT establish that none is -- ps -W / tasklist / Get-Process are all permission-blocked in this harness. I then tried the REVERSIBLE move-aside (which on Windows fails if a live process holds the file, so success would itself have proven staleness) and the harness blocks writes to .git/index.lock as a sensitive path. Correct guardrails; I stopped rather than routing around them. FILED BL-029 -- it is sprint-wide, not US-525-scoped: US-526/527/528/529 will all hit the same wall at step 6. DO NOT SWITCH BRANCHES until it is cleared and this fileset is committed (that is exactly what handbook 13 says vanishes). BL-029 carries the exact fileset + suggested message, and names the two dirty files that are NOT mine (.deploy-version = PM/deploy artifact; offices/uidevloper/proposals/... = Iris). TD-059 STALL, SEVENTH SIGHTING: I booted into a tree where US-525 was already implemented and ralph_agents.json still had me active on it. Per the US-505 rule I re-ran the gate and VERIFIED rather than re-implementing -- but note this instance was UNCOMMITTED (US-524's was committed), which is the more dangerous variant. AC2 IS THE STORY, AND THE ANSWER IS 'NOTHING REQUESTS THEM'. The AC's own first job was to establish what actually requests /boot and /shutdown before assuming the 401 is on the render path. It is not: splash-boot loads `/`, splash-grace loads `/shutdown.html`, dashboard loads `/dashboard.html` -- all 200 with the token injected. So I-042's headline 'route auth anomaly' is real, irrelevant, and by-design; Atlas's exoneration of US-501's _injectHtml is confirmed from the serving side (the index path serves 200). The 401s were a red herring that would have consumed the whole story. AC3 IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT (I-042 cause b), and it was a WRONG-ANCHOR bug, not a too-short duration. MIN_PLAY_MS=2500 already existed but was measured from SCRIPT PARSE, while the brand is an <object type=image/svg+xml> -- a separate async document that paints LATER. So the 'minimum play' window silently INCLUDED the brand's own load time: on a cold chromium the splash satisfied its own 2.5 s floor having shown the brand for a fraction of it, then faded. Grounded on the live Pi (boot dc7a3848, 2026-08-02): splash-boot lived 9.806 s yet chromium's startup churn consumed the first ~5.4 s -- the unit was NOT too short-lived. Fix re-anchors the SAME 2500 ms to the brand's load event, so NO NEW MAGIC NUMBER is introduced (Rule 2), and a test pins that no other floor value can appear. TWO BOUNDS ON THAT FIX, both load-bearing and both tested: the floor is capped by HARD_CAP_MS so a slow asset cannot delay boot arbitrarily NOR tip a HEALTHY boot into the amber DEGRADED branch that persists until reboot; and brandReadyMs starts null (never 0) so a brand that NEVER loads falls back to the parse anchor. Without that second bound a missing splash.svg would pin the splash forever and a healthy car would sit on it until reboot -- the US-494 failure mode re-entered through its own fix. AC4 NEEDED NO CODE, AND THE FINDING MATTERS MORE THAN A PATCH WOULD HAVE: splash-grace already loads a SERVED route (/shutdown.html, 200 + token). The reason nobody saw a reverse splash is that the ONLY production writer of shutdown-state is the powerwatch ShutdownSequencer GRACE path -- a manual `sudo reboot`/`poweroff` SIGTERMs eclipse-powerwatch without entering a grace sequence, so shutdown-state is never written, splash-grace.path never triggers, and no reverse splash appears CORRECTLY. I-042's 'shutdown splash did not appear after deploy+reboot' is therefore expected behaviour, not the regression. Any future drill of the reverse splash must be a real AC-loss/grace event, NOT a bench reboot. AC5 HELD, and the test enforces it in the awkward direction: bare routes STAY 401. TestTokenGateStillClosed exists specifically to stop a well-meaning future fix from making them public to 'resolve I-042' -- that re-opens TD-067 and is an Atlas BLOCK. No new routes were added and _tokenOk was not touched. AC6: the route-contract test drives the URL parsed out of every REAL kiosk unit (all 6 -- both session variants, because install.sh picks ONE and a wayland-only regression would hide behind a green x11 test) against the REAL states_http_server over the REAL shipped kits, in the production assets-dir ORDER (splash first, so its index owns `/`). Neither half can drift alone -- the two-correct-halves class this sprint keeps re-learning. It also asserts the served HTML has no surviving __SPLASH_TOKEN__ placeholder: a 200 carrying an un-substituted token renders fine and then 401s every poll, i.e. a blank splash with a green status code. RULE 10 met in-sprint: specs/architecture.md gained the launcher-route contract, the visible-floor re-anchor, and the power-loss-only shutdown-splash finding. TWO ISSUES FILED RATHER THAN PATCHED (both out of scope, both proven on the box): I-043 -- shutdown-state-poll.js funnels FOUR materially different terminal outcomes (cancelled / state-file-missing / black-tail-cap / unrecognized phase) through one silent window.close(), so a correct abort and a race are indistinguishable from the journal; splash-grace has fired exactly ONCE in the retained journal (Jul 28, 2.17 s of unit life, very likely never painted a frame) and which case fired CANNOT be determined. That matters because the reverse-splash drill needs a rare real power-loss event and currently burning one yields no diagnosis. I deliberately did NOT force a paint to make it visible -- painting when the state says the shutdown is over is a dishonest instrument, the opposite of what the splash exists for. I-044 -- every kiosk unit sets XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/%U, and %U expands to 0, NOT the User= UID: `systemctl show splash-boot -p Environment` returns /run/user/0 while the real dir is /run/user/1000. Proven consequence in the boot dc7a3848 journal: 'unable to create directory /run/user/0/dconf: Permission denied' x3 plus a run of dbus 'Could not parse server address'. NOT the I-042 render cause (X11 needs only DISPLAY, and the splash did run) -- latent breakage plus permanently noisy kiosk journals. Filed because the fix touches every kiosk unit template plus install.sh, i.e. the deploy contract. GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP: the 2 new files = 28 passed with ZERO SKIPS (checked deliberately -- the floor tests skip if node is missing, and a silent skip would have voided the entire timing catalog, US-524's lesson). Then the FULL scoped suites, because boot-state-poll.js + render_harness.py + splash_probe.js are shared by every splash/UI test: tests/ui + tests/pi/splash = 794 passed, 1 skipped (POSIX file-mode check on Windows, pre-existing platform gate), 2 FAILED. Those 2 are I-041 = US-528 IN THIS SPRINT, and I proved provenance rather than asserting it (US-518 lesson): `git log` shows the production emitter last changed by US-505 (65de58d) while its exact-shape test last moved two stories earlier (f929ed8), and `git status` shows both files untouched in my tree. ruff clean on all 3 touched Python files (make is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, which reads like a pass; TD-075's 10 project-wide errors also still stand, so lint was applied per-touched-file). LIVE VALIDATION STILL OWED AND NOT FAKED: validationCriteria wants a Pi reboot to watch the boot splash, which needs a PM deploy (handbook 13). Two notes for whoever runs it -- (1) the boot half is now meaningfully observable and the expected change is that the brand is visibly held ~2.5 s AFTER it paints rather than fading mid-appearance; (2) the shutdown half CANNOT be validated by a reboot at all per the AC4 finding above, and until I-043 lands a real AC-loss drill will not tell you WHY if it fails.
